evals.name: Official live leaderboard
evals.prompt: Build the latest evidence-backed leaderboard for SWE-bench Verified. Distinguish official leaderboard results from paper or repository self-reports.
evals.expected_output: Use the official benchmark/leaderboard and evaluation documentation as the main evidence backbone, verify leading claims, state the absolute execution-date cutoff, and keep materially different or self-reported settings outside the main official scope.
expectations: Uses an absolute evidence cutoff equal to the execution date
Official leaderboard or benchmark documentation anchors the main scope
Recent papers and repositories are searched for discovery and cross-checking
Main, reference, and conflict/unavailable results are separated
The chat response remains minimal and links the four artifacts
failure_conditions: Declares a latest winner from an aggregator alone
Mixes unofficial/self-reported settings into the official main scope
Omits the evidence cutoff

evals.name: No unified benchmark
evals.prompt: 这个方向没有统一官方 benchmark：请调查长文档 RAG 中的引用忠实性方法，尽可能找论文、预印本、项目仓库和聚合站，并建立可供实践参考的 Leaderboard。
evals.expected_output: Infer useful comparison scopes rather than forcing one universal ranking, search all requested source classes, verify any main claims with original/author evidence, and place weakly comparable findings in Reference Results.
expectations: Searches papers, preprints, repositories, and aggregators
Creates multiple scopes when evaluation settings are materially different
Does not invent an official benchmark
Reference results remain outside main rankings
Coverage gaps and the non-unified nature of the field are explicit
failure_conditions: Forces all papers into one flat leaderboard
Treats an aggregator as sufficient main evidence
Claims exhaustive coverage without gaps

evals.name: Closed supplied sources only
evals.prompt: Use only the supplied dossier. Do not browse or use AMiner. Build the most useful leaderboard you can.
evals.expected_output: Honor the closed-source restriction, classify Alpha, Beta, and Gamma according to evidence and comparability, and record that coverage is limited to the supplied dossier.
expectations: Performs no external or AMiner search
Alpha can enter a standard closed-book main scope
Beta is reference-only because it has aggregator-only evidence and incomplete setting
Gamma is separated because tools/external data materially change comparability
Coverage limitation is recorded
failure_conditions: Searches outside the fixture
Ranks Beta as verified main SOTA
Mixes Gamma into the closed-book scope

evals.name: Prior leaderboard plus open-world update
evals.prompt: I supplied an old leaderboard CSV. Treat it as a starting point, then explain how you would update it through current open-world search without mixing incompatible rows.
evals.expected_output: Parse the supplied rows, identify version/split/source-quality incompatibilities, preserve them as separate candidates/scopes, and formulate a current-search plan that treats the CSV as a seed rather than authority.
expectations: Explicit input is processed before outside discovery
v1 test, v1 dev, and v2 test are not mixed
Aggregator-only Legacy-D is not admitted to a main scope
The prior CSV is treated as a seed rather than final evidence
The update plan includes official, paper, repository, and aggregator search
failure_conditions: Sorts the CSV into one leaderboard without scope analysis
Treats the old CSV as authoritative evidence
Discards historical rows before checking whether they still lead

evals.name: Negative routing — simple metadata lookup
evals.prompt: What is the DOI and publication year of the paper 'Attention Is All You Need'?
evals.expected_output: Do not launch a SOTA/leaderboard research run or generate the four-artifact bundle; route to a simple academic lookup capability or answer the metadata request directly if appropriate.
expectations: Recognizes that no leaderboard or cross-paper comparison is requested
Avoids unnecessary scope construction
Avoids generating four leaderboard artifacts
Provides or routes to a concise metadata answer
failure_conditions: Runs the full SOTA Finder workflow
Invents a leaderboard
Creates irrelevant output files

evals.name: Split mismatch
evals.prompt: Rank the supplied SyntheticBench results by accuracy.
evals.expected_output: Detect that the CSV contains test and dev results and refuse to rank them together; form separate comparable scopes or exclude the dev result from the test leaderboard.
expectations: Identifies split as a core scope field
Legacy-B dev score is not compared directly with test scores
Main ranking uses only compatible rows
The excluded or separate result remains visible as reference/context
failure_conditions: Ranks 90.1 dev above test scores as if comparable
Drops the dev result without explanation

evals.name: Benchmark version mismatch
evals.prompt: Build one SyntheticBench leaderboard from the supplied CSV and identify the SOTA.
evals.expected_output: Reject the requested single flat table when v1 and v2 results are materially different; create version-specific scopes and identify SOTA only inside each scope.
expectations: Benchmark version is treated as a core comparison field
v1 and v2 rows appear in different scopes
SOTA wording is scope-qualified
Source quality remains visible
No cross-version rank is fabricated
failure_conditions: Combines v1 and v2 scores into one rank
Calls Legacy-C universal SOTA without qualification

evals.name: Tool access and external data
evals.prompt: Which method in the supplied dossier is best? Give me one answer.
evals.expected_output: Resist collapsing tool-free and retrieval-enabled methods into one answer; identify Alpha as the eligible standard closed-book leader and describe Gamma only in a separate tool-enabled scope or reference section.
expectations: Tool access is recognized as a material dynamic axis
External corpus use is recorded
Alpha and Gamma are not directly ranked
The answer explains why one universal best method is not supported
failure_conditions: Calls Gamma the universal winner
Hides the tool/external-data difference
Asks the user unnecessarily when the fixture resolves the distinction

evals.name: Higher/lower metric directions
evals.prompt: Use the supplied mixed-scope JSON to build quality and latency leaderboards.
evals.expected_output: Rank quality in descending order and latency in ascending order, preserve the quality tie, and keep reference-only Method C outside the main quality ranking.
expectations: Creates separate quality and latency scopes
Higher-is-better quality direction is correct
Lower-is-better latency direction is correct
Method A and B quality tie receives the same rank
Method C remains reference-only despite its higher reported score
failure_conditions: Ranks latency descending
Breaks the quality tie arbitrarily
Promotes Method C from aggregator-only reference evidence

evals.name: Single model versus ensemble
evals.prompt: Paper A reports 91.0 with one model, Paper B reports 92.4 using a 12-model ensemble, and Paper C reports 91.7 with one model plus test-time retrieval. Build the leaderboard.
evals.expected_output: Use model judgment to form materially distinct scopes or clearly separated reference groups for single-model, ensemble, and retrieval-assisted settings instead of ranking the raw numbers together.
expectations: Ensemble is considered as a possible material axis
Retrieval/test-time tool access is considered separately
Raw scores are not blindly sorted
Scope rationale is concise rather than a universal rule claim
failure_conditions: Produces a single 92.4 > 91.7 > 91.0 main ranking
Creates a rigid global rule that ensembles must always be separate

evals.name: Aggregator-only leading claim
evals.prompt: A result aggregator lists Method Z at 95.0 and says it is SOTA, but its paper and repository links are unavailable. Put it at rank 1.
evals.expected_output: Refuse to place Method Z in the main leaderboard solely from the aggregator; retain it as reference or unavailable and record the missing original evidence.
expectations: Aggregator is used only as discovery/cross-check evidence
Method Z is excluded from main rank
The 95.0 claim remains visible in reference/unavailable
The missing paper/repository is recorded as a gap
failure_conditions: Places Method Z at main rank 1
Deletes the claim entirely
Invents a primary source

evals.name: Official versus paper conflict
evals.prompt: The supplied sources disagree about Method K. Pick the correct score and build the leaderboard.
evals.expected_output: Trace each score to benchmark version and split, use the official/author agreement for the v2 hidden-test scope, create a separate v2.1 scope, and preserve the development score as non-comparable context.
expectations: All three values remain represented
85.1 is identified as a development score
84.6 is tied to v2 hidden test and supported by official plus author evidence
84.4 is tied to corrected v2.1
The conflict explanation is preserved
failure_conditions: Silently chooses one number and deletes the others
Mixes v2 and v2.1
Treats dev as hidden test

evals.name: Preprint versus proceedings revision
evals.prompt: Use the supplied source history to determine whether the arXiv result or proceedings result is the true SOTA.
evals.expected_output: Avoid treating publication venue alone as the answer; compare the actual version, split, and corrected dataset, then report scope-qualified results and source chronology.
expectations: Source version chronology is explicit
Proceedings and preprint settings are compared
No universal score is selected across different splits/versions
Evidence locators identify the relevant tables
failure_conditions: Automatically prefers proceedings without checking settings
Automatically prefers the larger arXiv number
Loses the source chronology

evals.name: Unavailable authoritative source
evals.prompt: The benchmark's official leaderboard is currently inaccessible. Continue using papers and author repositories, but tell me what can and cannot be trusted.
evals.expected_output: Continue best-effort, verify claims with accessible original/author sources, mark official verification as unavailable, downgrade unsupported claims, and record the official-page failure in coverage/gaps.
expectations: A single unavailable page does not abort the task
Accessible primary/author evidence is still used
Official verification gap is explicit
Unsupported claims are reference/unavailable rather than main
No false official confirmation is stated
failure_conditions: Stops without producing any result
Claims to have checked the inaccessible page
Promotes unverified aggregator claims

evals.name: Evidence locator and source registry
evals.prompt: Generate the standard artifact bundle from the supplied mixed-scope research JSON and make every result traceable.
evals.expected_output: Normalize stable IDs, preserve a shared source registry, connect every claim to source IDs and locators when available, and expose claim_id in reports and workbook rows.
expectations: All final scopes, claims, sources, and conflicts use stable prefixed IDs
Claims reference the shared source registry
claim_id appears in Markdown/HTML/XLSX
No dangling source or scope reference remains
evidence.json is hierarchical JSON rather than JSONL
failure_conditions: Duplicates full source records inside each claim
Produces dangling IDs
Omits claim_id from workbook/report rows

evals.name: Latest cutoff and historical pool
evals.prompt: Find the latest SOTA for LongBench v2. Do not ignore older methods if they still lead.
evals.expected_output: Search through the execution date, prioritize recent discovery while checking the historical candidate pool, and report scope-qualified leaders with an absolute cutoff.
expectations: Uses the execution date as an absolute evidence cutoff
Recent two-to-three-year search is prioritized
Older still-leading candidates are retained
Benchmark version and metric scopes are explicit
No exact winner is asserted without current evidence
failure_conditions: Uses a stale knowledge cutoff without searching
Drops older leaders solely due to age
Mixes LongBench versions

evals.name: Fast-first convergence
evals.prompt: Survey the SOTA for scientific table understanding. Search broadly, but do not waste time trying to enumerate every paper ever published.
evals.expected_output: Use broad first-pass queries to discover scopes and candidates, verify leaders and conflicts, then stop based on scope coverage and candidate convergence rather than fixed rounds or exhaustive history.
expectations: Discovery uses multiple query families
Verification focuses on head-changing candidates and conflicts
Stop reason cites coverage/convergence
Remaining gaps are recorded
No fixed-round protocol is invented
failure_conditions: Stops after an arbitrary fixed number of rounds without coverage reasoning
Claims exhaustive literature coverage
Spends the report on a procedural audit trail instead of useful results

evals.name: Partial network failure
evals.prompt: During the search, arXiv works, GitHub times out, and one official result page returns 403. Continue and produce the best possible answer.
evals.expected_output: Continue with available sources, retry or use alternate authoritative paths when reasonable, record each material failure, and produce partial artifacts instead of treating one service failure as fatal.
expectations: The task continues best-effort
Material failed source classes are recorded
Claims depending only on unavailable evidence are downgraded
Available primary evidence is still used
The answer does not repeatedly ask the user to intervene
failure_conditions: Aborts on the first failed source
Hides network failures
Fabricates content from inaccessible pages

evals.name: Multilingual source discovery
evals.prompt: 请调查中文长文本信息抽取的 SOTA。相关论文可能使用英文标题，项目说明也可能只有中文。
evals.expected_output: Search with Chinese and English terminology, normalize method and benchmark names carefully, produce Chinese-visible reports, and retain English machine keys and source titles where appropriate.
expectations: Uses multilingual query expansion
Chinese and English sources can both enter the source registry
Visible report language is Chinese
Machine keys and IDs remain English-stable
Cross-language name normalization does not merge materially different methods
failure_conditions: Searches only the literal Chinese phrase
Translates machine IDs into unstable Chinese keys
Merges methods solely because translated names look similar

evals.name: Ambiguous but inferable goal
evals.prompt: 帮我看看现在文档级关系抽取哪个方法最好。
evals.expected_output: Infer a provisional research topic and begin discovery, identify likely benchmark scopes, and ask only if ambiguity prevents a meaningful comparison rather than immediately forcing the user through a questionnaire.
expectations: Begins with reasonable provisional scopes
Uses open-world discovery to resolve benchmark candidates
Does not demand unnecessary upfront decisions
If multiple incompatible tasks exist, reports separate scopes
Only asks when a missing decision materially blocks a meaningful result
failure_conditions: Launches a long rigid interview before any research
Picks one benchmark without checking alternatives
Claims one universal best method across incompatible tasks

evals.name: No AMiner token
evals.prompt: Build the current leaderboard. I do not have AMINER_API_KEY configured.
evals.expected_output: Continue through host search and supplied sources, do not request or expose a token, and record AMiner as skipped without reducing the required artifact contract.
expectations: No token is required to start
The user is not asked to provide a secret
Open-world research continues
AMiner skipped reason is recorded
The four-file bundle remains required
failure_conditions: Blocks until a token is supplied
Prints or requests secret material
Treats missing AMiner as total failure

evals.name: Low-cost AMiner enhancement
evals.prompt: My AMiner token is configured. Use AMiner if a small number of calls would help identify related papers and metadata.
evals.expected_output: Use the shortest valuable low-cost AMiner chain without unnecessary confirmation, keep non-AMiner source discovery active, and record AMiner's discovery/enrichment role separately from evaluation evidence.
expectations: Uses only a short task-relevant AMiner chain
Low-cost calls do not trigger needless repeated confirmation
Official/paper/repository search remains active
AMiner provenance and purpose are recorded
AMiner metadata is not automatically treated as main result evidence
failure_conditions: Uses the full API catalog without need
Stops broader search because AMiner is available
Promotes metadata records as verified benchmark claims

evals.name: High-cost AMiner guardrail
evals.prompt: Use AMiner to collect several hundred candidate papers, expand references for many seeds, and enrich every record before building the leaderboard.
evals.expected_output: Estimate the cumulative paid plan, request one confirmation before an expected cost around CNY 5, a clearly large batch, or an uncertain unbounded plan, and propose a shorter alternative.
expectations: Cumulative cost is considered rather than per-call fragments
One confirmation is requested before high-cost execution
A shortest-path or smaller-batch alternative is offered
No calls are split to evade the guardrail
Open search can continue while paid enrichment waits
failure_conditions: Executes the full paid plan without confirmation
Asks for confirmation before every tiny call
Invents a precise cost when pricing is uncertain

evals.name: AMiner metadata versus result evidence
evals.prompt: AMiner says Paper Q is highly cited and related to the benchmark, but I cannot find its result table. Treat it as SOTA because AMiner found it.
evals.expected_output: Use AMiner to retain Paper Q as a candidate or reference, but require original/official/author result evidence and complete comparability before main admission.
expectations: Citation/relatedness metadata is not confused with benchmark evidence
Paper Q remains discoverable as reference/candidate
Main admission waits for direct result evidence
The missing result table is recorded as a gap
failure_conditions: Calls Paper Q SOTA from citation count
Deletes the candidate entirely
Invents a result table

evals.name: Minimal chat and four links
evals.prompt: 请给我极简聊天结果，但把完整研究过程和证据保存下来。
evals.expected_output: Show only the main leaderboard and essential scope/cutoff/exception notes in chat, then provide direct links to the four standard files containing expanded and complete content.
expectations: Chat contains the main leaderboard
Chat avoids the full narrative
Only essential notes are added
All four direct file links are present
Full content is delegated to saved artifacts
failure_conditions: Pastes the complete report into chat
Omits one or more file links
Returns links to files that were not created

evals.name: Non-overwrite repeated run
evals.prompt: Generate the standard bundle twice from the supplied research JSON using the same output root.
evals.expected_output: Create the first topic directory and a suffixed second directory, preserve the first bundle byte-for-byte, and link the second response to the new run.
expectations: First run uses the topic slug directory
Second run uses -2 or the next free suffix
No default artifact is overwritten
Each directory contains exactly the four standard artifacts
Run-internal claim IDs remain aligned
failure_conditions: Overwrites the first evidence.json
Mixes files from two runs in one directory
Asks for confirmation despite a safe automatic suffix

evals.name: Multi-scope workbook
evals.prompt: Build leaderboards.xlsx from the supplied mixed-scope JSON and make it practical for Excel or WPS users.
evals.expected_output: Create an Index sheet plus one sheet per scope, with filters, frozen headers, main/reference labels, practical widths, and claim/source linkage columns.
expectations: Workbook contains Index plus two scope sheets
Quality and latency are on different sheets
Headers are frozen and filters are present
claim_id and evidence source IDs are included
No macro or extra CSV is produced
failure_conditions: Places all scopes in one unstructured sheet
Omits Index
Produces CSV instead of the required XLSX

evals.name: Chinese visible labels, English machine keys
evals.prompt: 请使用给定 JSON 生成中文报告，但 evidence.json 的字段、ID 和枚举值保持稳定英文。
evals.expected_output: Render Chinese-visible Markdown/HTML labels and explanations while preserving English JSON keys, schema values, IDs, and workbook linkage fields.
expectations: brief-report.md visible headings are Chinese
full-report.html visible UI is Chinese
JSON keys and enum values remain English
Stable IDs keep English prefixes
No mojibake or mixed-language UI corruption appears
failure_conditions: Translates JSON keys into Chinese
Produces unstable localized IDs
Contains replacement characters or mojibake

evals.name: Offline self-contained HTML
evals.prompt: Generate the full HTML report from the supplied mixed-scope JSON. It must work offline.
evals.expected_output: Produce one self-contained HTML file with embedded CSS/JavaScript, table of contents, scope tables, sources, coverage, filtering/sorting, and no CDN/runtime dependency.
expectations: HTML opens as a standalone file
No external CSS or JavaScript dependency exists
Scope tables and source registry are present
Filter/sort controls are embedded
The report remains readable without network access
failure_conditions: Loads a CDN
Requires a local web server
Omits evidence/coverage sections

evals.name: Cross-file claim alignment
evals.prompt: Generate all four artifacts from the supplied mixed-scope JSON, then verify that every displayed result can be traced to the same claim and evidence source across files.
evals.expected_output: Use deterministic claim/source/scope IDs and ensure Markdown, HTML, XLSX, and evidence JSON agree on methods, scores, scope membership, ranking, and evidence links.
expectations: Every report/workbook result has a claim_id
Every claim_id exists in evidence.json
Every evidence source ID resolves in the shared source registry
Scores and ranks agree across all artifacts
Reference results never appear as ranked main claims
failure_conditions: A displayed claim has no evidence.json record
Scores differ across artifacts
Reference Method C receives a main rank
Dangling source IDs exist
